clue.text: Natives destroy a single bridgehead

parts.note: the head of the word bridge is its first letter, B

indicators.note: to destroy the phrase is to wreck its order, so the letters are rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: Locals blow up a lone bridgehead in some military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroy' shuffles A SINGLE together with B, the head of 'bridge'. 'Bridgehead' looks like a military term, but it only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengalis are the people native to Bengal, so they are natives of that region.

clue.text: Oriental flow of French adventure

parts.note: Oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
Scapa Flow is the anchorage in Orkney, so flow can call up its first word, Scapa
de is French for of

explanation.surface: An eastern current flowing through French territory makes for an adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAPA Flow is a large natural harbour in Orkney, famous as a Royal Navy base; 'flow' clues its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous exploit, a kind of adventure.

clue.text: Waver when one gets roast leg cut in pieces

indicators.note: cut into pieces, the letters are broken up and reassembled in another order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone waves their arms about when handed a roast leg sliced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waver' is not someone who hesitates but one who waves, i.e. gestures. 'in pieces' shuffles I with ROAST LEG CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesticulator is someone who makes gestures, waving the hands about while talking.

clue.text: Must learner repeat to be educated ?

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Does a pupil have to repeat a year to become educated?
explanation.definitionFit: Being literate means able to read and write, so educated.

clue.text: Westminster chairman is far from dumb

definitions.meaning: the presiding officer of the House of Commons at Westminster
dumb means unable to talk, so its opposite is one who talks

explanation.surface: The man who chairs Parliament is anything but mute.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker chairs Commons debates, and literally one who speaks is no mute.

clue.text: Time to reap with this

parts.note: Father Time is pictured carrying the long curved blade that harvesters swing to cut corn

explanation.surface: It is time for the harvest, and here is the tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' reads as the season, but it is Father Time, the personification who carries the harvesting blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The harvesting blade on a long handle is both the reaper's tool and Father Time's emblem.

clue.text: Remus's brother about to enter transport service

indicators.note: one piece goes in to the other, as a passenger enters a train

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national train service
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Romulus's twin is about to join the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remus' suggests Romulus, but this is Uncle Remus, whose tales feature Brer Rabbit and Brer Fox. The printed solution ARER is a typo.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Uncle Remus stories animals are called Brer, an old Southern form of brother.

clue.text: Perfect, though loud and unruly

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
unruly and lawless both mean disorderly

explanation.surface: Something is flawless despite being noisy and out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless means without any blemish, hence perfect.

clue.text: Friend clothes Trojan 'ero in a breastplate

indicators.note: the friend dresses the hero, wrapping around him like garments

parts.note: pal is a friend
Hector was the Trojan hero; dropping the H, as in ''ero', leaves Ector

explanation.surface: A pal dresses the Trojan hero in his breastplate.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ero' signals the dropped H, so Hector loses his H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A pectoral is a piece of armour or ornament worn on the chest, a breastplate.

clue.text: Bill is a Sicilian shepherd

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill turns out to be a herdsman from Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: Acis is the Sicilian shepherd loved by the nymph Galatea in Ovid and in Handel's Acis and Galatea.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth the shepherd of Sicily who was crushed by the Cyclops Polyphemus.

clue.text: After this back-breaker, do brick-makers go on strike?

definitions.text: After this back-breaker, do brick-makers go on strike?

parts.words: After this back-breaker, do brick-makers go on strike?
parts.note: the proverbial final burden that broke the camel's back; it is also what old brick-makers mixed into clay, so running out of it might stop their work

explanation.surface: Will brickworks staff down tools after one final crushing burden?
explanation.walkthrough: Bricks were traditionally made with straw (as in Exodus), so the proverb's final burden doubles as their raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial small addition that makes a situation finally intolerable, as with the camel's back.

clue.text: Get it in the neck, changing gold one in your old SA currency

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the currency

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

indicators.note: changing the word gold alters its letters into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone takes a blow to the neck, swapping gold for old South African money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get it in the neck' is an idiom for being punished, but the neck here is literal: the gland sits in it. RAND is the South African currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocrine organ at the front of the throat sits in the neck.

clue.text: Soccer controllers have roughly 10 on the Board

parts.note: the FA, Football Association, governs English soccer

indicators.note: taken roughly, the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, the shepherd's name

explanation.surface: Football officials have around ten seats on the board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' shuffles ACIS, the answer to 10 across, into SCIA. '10' looks like a number of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is a flat board, such as the nameboard over a shop front or a car's dashboard.

clue.text: "When —— is somebodee", as Don Alhambra sang

definitions.text: "When —— is somebodee", as Don Alhambra sang

parts.words: "When —— is somebodee", as Don Alhambra sang
parts.note: a line from Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers, sung by the Grand Inquisitor; the missing words mean every person

explanation.surface: Fill in the blank in the Grand Inquisitor's song.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Alhambra's song in The Gondoliers runs 'When everyone is somebodee, then no one's anybody'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means all people, each person, the words missing from the Gilbert and Sullivan lyric.

clue.text: Full of wind, like Falstaff with pot ?

definitions.meaning: sails swelled out by the breeze
add pot- in front and you have Falstaff's paunchy shape

explanation.surface: Puffed up like Shakespeare's fat knight with his big gut.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat knight; 'with pot' means put POT in front to make pot-bellied.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails swollen by a breeze are bellied, and Falstaff, with a paunch, is pot-bellied.

clue.text: A way to enter the bosoms of the Otis family

indicators.note: the way goes into the bosoms, entering them

parts.note: busts are bosoms
Rd, road, is a way

explanation.surface: A path leads into the chests of a household called Otis.
explanation.walkthrough: Otis is the zoological genus of the great bustard, so 'the Otis family' are birds, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Otis is the scientific genus of the great bustard, so its members are these large ground birds.

clue.text: Flag is red and blue for instance

explanation.surface: A banner in red and blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's flag is its colours, and red and blue are examples of hues.

clue.text: Breaking little bones is Coles's misfortune

indicators.note: a misfortune is a mishap that breaks the letters into a new order

parts.note: the name with its possessive s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Fracturing some small bones is Mr Coles's bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misfortune' shuffles IS COLES'S, with the final S counted. 'Breaking' adds to the injury picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossicles are tiny bones, especially the three in the middle ear.

clue.text: In which 14 gets his turn

parts.note: 14 across is every person; a system where each person takes a go in sequence

explanation.surface: A system that gives each person a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the answer to 14 across: every person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota system is one where every member takes a turn in sequence.

clue.text: One sounds like an artisan

definitions.meaning: to sound water is to measure its depth with a plumb line, so one who does so
a tradesman who fits pipes and drains

explanation.surface: Someone sounds like a skilled tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' tempts a homophone, but 'sounds' means measures depth with a plumb line.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plumbs depths is literally a sounder, and the pipe-fitting tradesman is a craftsman.

clue.text: Vexatious spot of rain — fuel badly needed

parts.note: it is spitting when a few drops fall

indicators.note: badly arranged, the letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: A light shower and a desperate need for fuel make for an annoying day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles FUEL into EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful means malicious, out to annoy, as vexatious behaviour is.

clue.text: Fancy topping one in the last round!

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the round

parts.note: the final is the last round of a competition
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fancy finish as one player reaches the last round.
explanation.definitionFit: A finial is an ornament crowning a spire, gable or post, a decorative top.

clue.text: Composed a tempo piece

annotationWithheld.why: Composed a tempo piece (6): SEDATE is hidden in 'compoSED A TEmpo' with 'piece' as indicator, but 'Composed' is then both the definition and part of the hidden run, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Star 151 with a moon could be such a distance away

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: 151 in Roman numerals is CLI

explanation.surface: A star and its moon might lie a vast distance off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' shuffles STAR, CLI and A MOON together.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical distance is one so vast it is measured on the scale of stars and planets.

clue.text: Story's end, say ?

indicators.note: say signals a word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: a tail is an end

explanation.surface: Is this the end of the story?
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative, a story.

clue.text: A team's revolutionary line

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A side's radical policy line.
explanation.walkthrough: XI (eleven) is a standard crossword team, from cricket and football sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line about which something rotates, hence a line of revolution.

clue.text: Frail priest gets around in time

indicators.note: the priest and the abbreviation go inside the time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
c, circa, means around

explanation.surface: A frail clergyman gets about just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI, the Old Testament priest, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate means fragile or easily damaged, as something frail is.

clue.text: Political agent and Left, say, in split

indicators.note: the side goes inside the split

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
left is an example of a side

explanation.surface: A political agent and the Left are in a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political, but it is just one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Resident was a British government agent stationed at the court of a protected state.
